column2: ENGLISH
Prepare for the General Synod
Consult your bishops and try to shape the agenda of the coming General Synod. Secular rulers influence their clergy but do not vote in the assembly.
I will speak with my bishops.
Choose a method of influence and recommend an agenda to your bishops. Rank and the chosen method determine the strength of your influence.
Preparations for a General Synod

Letters sealed by the Synodal Chancery have gone out from [d_synodal.Holder.Location.GetName]. The bishops are summoned to prayer, consultation, and common judgment. As Presiding Prelate, I must arrange their assembly and faithfully proclaim whatever the fathers decide.
Let the churches prepare their delegates.
The Bishops Have Been Summoned

The Synodal Chancery announces that a General Synod will soon assemble at [d_synodal.Holder.Location.GetName]. I possess no vote in the council of bishops, but my own prelates will listen if I petition, persuade, patronize, or pressure them.
I will consult my bishops.
The fathers must judge without my interference.
Influencing the Fathers

My bishops prepare their petitions and arguments. I may appeal to conscience, fund the journey and works of the Church, invoke the needs of the realm, or compel obedience. The more worldly methods carry a greater danger of scandal.
Persuade them with pious argument.
Provide generous patronage for their work.
Remind them of political realities.
Their obedience will be assured.
On reflection, I shall do nothing.
A Petition to the General Synod
My clergy ask what cause they should commend to the assembled fathers. They remain free to judge, but a clear petition from their ruler will carry weight in their deliberations.
Defend the faithful and their homes.
Send missions to the scattered churches.
Reform the discipline of the clergy.
Confirm [d_synodal.Holder.Location.GetName] and the present Prelate.
The General Synod Concludes

With extraordinary attendance and a clear common judgment, the fathers rise together in prayer. The Presiding Prelate proclaims their decree to the churches, and the faithful acclaim a triumph of unity.
After prayer and measured debate, the bishops reach a broad agreement. The Presiding Prelate proclaims the decision of the fathers, and the churches receive it in peace.
The bishops reach a decision only after sharp debate and close votes. The Presiding Prelate proclaims the judgment of the assembly, though several churches record their reservations.
The petitions cannot be reconciled and no stable majority forms. The fathers adjourn without an effective decree, while the Synodal Chancery quietly prepares for an earlier return to council.
Evidence of gifts, threats, and worldly interference overshadows the deliberations. Whatever the merits of the adopted petition, the churches speak more of scandal than unity.
The churches must prepare to meet again.
The Synod has judged that the faithful must be defended.
The Synod sends new missions to the scattered faithful.
The Synod commands a reform of clerical discipline.
The Synod confirms [d_synodal.Holder.Location.GetName] and the Presiding Prelate.
Recent General Synod
The churches will not be summoned to another ordinary General Synod until this cooldown expires.
General Synod in Preparation
Delegates and petitions are being prepared for the coming General Synod.
Defense of the Faithful
The General Synod has urged rulers and bishops to protect threatened Synodal communities.
Synodal Missionary Priority
The General Synod has made the support of missions a priority for the churches.
Mandate to the Missions
This chaplain has received the Synod's mandate to strengthen scattered churches and preach the faith.
Synodal Clerical Reform
The ruler publicly supports the General Synod's decrees on clerical discipline.
Renewed Clerical Discipline
This bishop has accepted the Synod's call to learning, virtue, and discipline.
Confirmed by the General Synod
The assembled bishops have confirmed this Presiding Prelate and [d_synodal.Holder.Location.GetName]'s place as the current Synodal seat.
Exposed Synodal Manipulator
This ruler's worldly interference in the General Synod became a public scandal.
